_what_this_is: Second access pass over the 35 records coded unreachable_paywalled in the four SEALED reserve blocks (paper/screen_reserve_R{1,2,3,4}.json). Those blocks had had only one access pass, unlike the four main batches, whose second pass is recorded in paper/screen/access_recovery.json. Machine endpoints were worked first, then aggregators, then repositories and preprint servers.
_does_not_edit_sealed_files: paper/screen_reserve_R{1,2,3,4}.json are the screeners' sealed, git-timestamped submissions and are NOT modified by this pass. This file is an overlay to be applied at analysis time, in the same manner as paper/screen/access_recovery.json.
_operator: access-recovery pass over the reserve blocks, agent-executed, single operator
_sources_permitted: PubMed Central / Europe PMC REST; the PMC OA Web Service; Unpaywall; OpenAlex; Semantic Scholar; Crossref; CORE; OpenAIRE; BASE; arXiv; figshare; publisher OA pages; institutional and subject repositories; and the Internet Archive Wayback Machine as a public archive of documents that are themselves openly licensed.
_sources_refused: Sci-Hub, LibGen and every other unauthorised full-text source. None was fetched, not even to test availability. No record below is reported as reachable because such a source holds it. Bot-detection and Cloudflare challenges were NOT circumvented: where a site refused this environment, that is recorded as an environment limitation and the record stays unreachable unless a legitimate alternate copy existed. HKUST's institutional repository was NOT crawled because its robots.txt disallows /ir/search/ for non-whitelisted agents.

_ladder_rerun_summary.note: One record recovered, 38324428, and it proves ELIGIBLE on full text, so it moves from the unreachable column into the included column and the eligible-looking denominator is unchanged at 111.

_endpoints_that_worked: Crossref query.bibliographic title search -- THE DISCOVERY ENDPOINT. It was the only source that revealed the existence of the TechRxiv preprint DOI 10.36227/techrxiv.19750774.v1 for record 38324428. Unpaywall, OpenAlex and Europe PMC all independently reported that record as closed with zero OA locations.

Internet Archive Wayback Machine, raw ('id_') mode against an archived 302 -- THE DELIVERY ENDPOINT. The only endpoint in this entire pass that returned a readable full text. The live TechRxiv site 403s and the figshare object it redirected to has since been deleted, so the Wayback copy is now the only reachable copy of an openly licensed document.
figshare API -- returned the ACS Supporting Information for 40644803 under CC BY-NC 4.0. This is a PARTIAL result: the supplement only, not the article body.

_endpoints_that_returned_nothing.pmc_oa_web_service: Not applicable to a single one of the 35. NCBI's ID converter reports 'Identifier not found in PMC' for every record, and Europe PMC returns pmcid=null and inEPMC=N for every record. The PMC OA Web Service was the single most likely win named in the brief; it cannot help here because none of these 35 papers is in PMC at all.
_endpoints_that_returned_nothing.europepmc_fullTextXML: HTTP 404 for all 35 on both the MED and PMC routes.
_endpoints_that_returned_nothing.europepmc_supplementaryFiles: hasSuppl=N for effectively all; nothing retrieved.
_endpoints_that_returned_nothing.europepmc_preprint_PPR: no preprint indexed for any of the 35.
_endpoints_that_returned_nothing.unpaywall: 33 of 35 oa_status=closed with zero OA locations. The 2 exceptions are both dead ends and are described in _traps_for_the_next_pass.
_endpoints_that_returned_nothing.openalex: agreed with Unpaywall on all 35; surfaced no location Unpaywall lacked.
_endpoints_that_returned_nothing.semantic_scholar: 4 records carried a non-empty openAccessPdf. 2 were dead at source, 1 was an Elsevier accepted manuscript behind a 403, and 1 (38324428) pointed at the deleted figshare object that the Wayback route ultimately recovered.
_endpoints_that_returned_nothing.arxiv: no title match for any of the 35. NOTE: in an earlier attempt 15 of the 35 arXiv queries silently returned HTTP 429 and were never actually searched; the sweep was re-run with rate limiting and all 35 returned HTTP 200 before this conclusion was drawn.
_endpoints_that_returned_nothing.core: 1 metadata record only (36403310, deposited by the HKUST institutional repository); its downloadUrl returns HTTP 404 and no full text exists at CORE. NOTE: an earlier attempt used a title:"..." query that CORE did not parse as a filter and that returned the entire 88.6M-record corpus; the pass was re-run querying by DOI before this conclusion was drawn.
_endpoints_that_returned_nothing.base: unusable from this environment -- BASE returned 'Access denied for IP address ... and user agent ...'. BASE requires a registered IP. Recorded as an environment limitation, not as evidence of absence.

_traps_for_the_next_pass.trap: Unpaywall and OpenAlex both report is_oa=true, oa_status=green, version=submittedVersion, licence cc-by-nc-nd, at the Fujita Health University repository. A pass that trusted the metadata would score this as RECOVERED. It is not. The deposited file is a single page and is the author's DOCTORAL DISSERTATION ABSTRACT in Japanese (title block: '論文内容の要旨', plus the thesis examination committee's report), not the Nuclear Medicine Communications article. It cannot support the mandatory 14-term search of body and supplement, so trivial_baseline stays not_assessable and the record stays unreachable.

The figshare title match is the ACS Supporting Information (DOI 10.1021/acsnano.5c02822.s001, file nn5c02822_si_001.pdf, CC BY-NC 4.0), NOT the article. The 13-page supplement WAS obtained and WAS 14-term searched, because a positive found in a supplement would still count. It contains no zero-image baseline: the only hits are two occurrences of 'Constant', both of which are the intercept row of a logistic-regression table, not a constant-class predictor. Because the article BODY was never obtained, the negative cannot be certified under the codebook and the record stays unreachable with trivial_baseline not_assessable.

_demonstrably_open_access_but_refused_by.evidence: Semantic Scholar reports an open-access accepted manuscript at https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/am/pii/S221253452200003X with status GREEN. Elsevier returns HTTP 403 to every client available here and there is no Wayback snapshot. Counted unreachable; the cause is this environment, not the literature.

Unpaywall and OpenAlex both report oa_status=hybrid, publishedVersion, licence cc-by-nc-nd, hosted by the publisher. The DOI resolves to ScienceDirect, which serves this environment a 2,664-byte interstitial rather than the article, and there is no Wayback snapshot. Counted unreachable; the cause is this environment, not the literature.

_primary_endpoint_effect.statement: The one fully recovered and fully coded record, 38324428, reports NO zero-image baseline of any kind. All six sub-flags are FALSE and the negative is evidenced by the complete 14-term search recorded in searches_run. The 13-page supplement of 40644803 was also fully 14-term searched and likewise contains no zero-image baseline. Across the reserve access-recovery pass the count of papers reporting a positional, constant/prevalence, acquisition-metadata or permuted-label baseline remains exactly ZERO.
_primary_endpoint_effect.reading_discipline: Each document was searched for a POSITIVE first and the absence certified only afterwards; every one of the 14 term hits in 38324428 and the 2 in the 40644803 supplement was read in context and adjudicated individually rather than dismissed in bulk.

recovered_and_recoded.citation: Weng L, Zhu Z, Wu H, Zhu J. Reduced-Reference Learning for Target Localization in Deep Brain Stimulation. IEEE Trans Med Imaging 2024. doi:10.1109/TMI.2024.3363425
recovered_and_recoded.access_rung_succeeded: rung 4 -- author preprint. TechRxiv posting 10.36227/techrxiv.19750774.v1, licence CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (licence asserted by Crossref on the TechRxiv DOI and printed on the document's own cover page: 'LICENSE CC BY-NC-SA 4.0'), retrieved from the Internet Archive Wayback Machine.
recovered_and_recoded.how_it_was_found: Crossref query.bibliographic title search returned a second DOI with an identical title, 10.36227/techrxiv.19750774.v1, type 'posted-content', publisher IEEE. Unpaywall, OpenAlex and Europe PMC ALL reported this record as closed with zero OA locations; none of them knew about the TechRxiv posting. Semantic Scholar's openAccessPdf independently pointed at the same figshare object but at a URL that is now dead.
recovered_and_recoded.access_channel_note: The live TechRxiv site (www.techrxiv.org) returns a Cloudflare interstitial and HTTP 403 to every client available in this environment; the challenge was NOT circumvented. TechRxiv's old figshare-backed object id 19750774 now 404s at api.figshare.com and ndownloader.figshare.com, so the Semantic Scholar OA link is dead at source. The document was obtained from the Internet Archive Wayback Machine, which had archived the file URL as a 302 in 2022; fetching that snapshot in raw mode (web.archive.org/web/20220518135002id_/...) returned the 1,983,861-byte PDF. This is a public archive of a document the authors themselves posted under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; it is not an unauthorised source.
recovered_and_recoded.fulltext_version_used: preprint (TechRxiv v1, posted 2022-05-17; the version of record is IEEE TMI 2024 and was NOT read)
recovered_and_recoded.document_read: 12-page TechRxiv preprint PDF, 50,090 characters of extracted text, complete main text from Abstract through References.
recovered_and_recoded.supplement_status: The preprint's own text refers to an appendix ('The groundtruth targets are determined by a DTI-based tractography process, as described in the appendix'), but NO appendix section is present in this 12-page v1 document -- it ends with the reference list. The 14-term search below therefore covers the COMPLETE MAIN TEXT of the preprint and NOT the referenced appendix, and not any supplement attached to the IEEE version of record. flag_for_adjudication is set on this ground and on the preprint-only ground.
recovered_and_recoded.eligibility_resolution: S1 recorded this record as genuinely undecidable from the abstract, because the abstract frames the task as regression ('we consider target localization as a non-linear regression problem') and reports only millimetre errors, which points to E-SEG, while also naming a classification network. THE FULL TEXT SETTLES IT IN FAVOUR OF INCLUSION. I2 is met: a supervised classifier is fitted over slices with a binary cross-entropy loss. I3 is met: the input is 2D slices of a 3T volumetric MRI acquisition. I4 is met: precision and recall are defined and reported numerically, and precision is PPV while recall is sensitivity, both of which are named metrics in I4. E-SEG does not apply because its own text is qualified 'with NO categorical class decision evaluated' and a class decision IS evaluated here; E-SEG further directs that where a paper does both, INCLUDE and code only the classification arm. Coded below: the classification arm only.
recovered_and_recoded.evaluation_unit_quote: "each MRI scan in the validation set is individually examined in a retrieval framework: slices are ranked according to the classification output; precision and recall are computed at each rank" (Sec. IV-C, Classification (Retrieval) Performance). The metric denominators are slices: "precision = no. of retrieved slices with targets / no. of retrieved slices" and "recall = no. of retrieved slices with targets / no. of all slices with targets" (Sec. IV-B, eqs. 9-10).
recovered_and_recoded.headline_unit_quote: The classification arm is scored only per slice; no patient-level classification metric is reported anywhere.
recovered_and_recoded.split_quote: "both datasets are split into a training set (127 subjects) and a validation set (32 subjects, about 20%)" (Sec. IV-A, The Datasets), and "32 subjects (among 159) are randomly chosen for validation and the rest is used for training" (Sec. IV-C). The split unit is the SUBJECT, not the slice.
recovered_and_recoded.trivial_baseline_quote: ALL SIX SUB-FLAGS FALSE, and the negative is evidenced. searches_run (below) was executed over the complete 50,090-character main text. Every hit was inspected and none is a pixel-free comparator with a measured value. 'baseline' x2 -- both metaphorical and forward-looking, no number attached: "may serve as a baseline for general target localization problems in DBS" (Abstract) and "our approach might serve as a framework and a baseline for other target localization problems in DBS" (Sec. V). 'chance' x1 -- colloquial: "which gives a chance for further variance reduction". 'random' x2 -- the validation split ("32 subjects (among 159) are randomly chosen for validation") and a cited randomised clinical trial in the reference list; NOT a permutation null. 'majority' x3 -- all descriptive of result distributions, e.g. "the majority (9/11) of slices with targets can be efficiently found" and "The majority (> 80%) is below 4 mm"; NOT a majority-class classifier. 'trivial' x1 -- algebraic: "Ignoring the trivial case WB = 0". 'location' x5 -- all substantive anatomical discussion of DBS target location. 'prevalence', 'constant', 'metadata', 'clinical-only', 'clinical model', 'position', 'slice index', 'permut' -- ZERO hits each. No constant/majority/prevalence predictor, no positional or slice-index model, no acquisition-metadata model, no permuted-label null, no clinical-only arm, and no other pixel-free comparator is reported anywhere in the document.
recovered_and_recoded.searches_run: Mandatory 14-term full-text search, codebook v1.2, run over the complete extracted text of the 12-page TechRxiv preprint (50,090 chars). baseline (2 hits); chance (1); random (2); majority (3); prevalence (0); constant (0); trivial (1); metadata (0); clinical-only (0); clinical model (0); position (0); location (5); slice index (0); permut (0). 14 hits total, every one inspected and adjudicated in trivial_baseline_quote. SCOPE LIMITATION: the appendix referred to in the text is not present in this preprint version, and the IEEE version-of-record supplement was not obtained.
recovered_and_recoded.positional_distribution_quote: The paper ranks slices by classifier score and reports precision@K and recall@K, but never reports the distribution of target-bearing slice indices within the stack; 'slice index' and 'position' both return ZERO hits in the 14-term search. Individual figure captions name slice numbers for single illustrative cases (e.g. "(a) subject 48, slice 108", Fig. 11) but no distribution over slice position is given. This is directly relevant to the present paper's own construction and was checked specifically.
recovered_and_recoded.dataset_name: Human Connectome Project, WU-Minn HCP Data - 1200 Subjects Release
recovered_and_recoded.n_slices_or_images: not stated as a total; two derived datasets (a classification dataset over all slices and a localization dataset restricted to slices with targets); 704 targets in the localization validation set (352 left, 352 right)
recovered_and_recoded.n_positive_reported: not stated for the classification dataset
recovered_and_recoded.headline_metric: precision@1 (equivalently PPV at rank 1) for the classification arm
recovered_and_recoded.headline_metric_qualifier: retrieval framing; "The average precision varies from 0.85 to 0.98, and generally decreases with K. In particular, precision@1 = 0.98". Recall reaches 0.848 at K = 11. The paper's own abstract-level headline is the LOCALIZATION error (2.3 mm mean, 1.7 mm median), which is a regression metric and is not the classification arm.
recovered_and_recoded.headline_value_scope: validation split, averaged over five rounds
recovered_and_recoded.headline_selection_rule: best-reported value at K=1, taken from the text
recovered_and_recoded.label_broadcast_to_slices: not_applicable -- slice labels are intrinsic (a slice either does or does not contain a target), not broadcast from a patient-level label
recovered_and_recoded.code_availability: not_stated (no code or repository statement anywhere in the preprint; 'github' and 'Code' both return zero hits)
recovered_and_recoded.screener_confidence: high on the trivial_baseline negative and on eligibility; moderate on headline_metric because the paper's own emphasis is the regression arm
recovered_and_recoded.flag_reason: Two independent grounds. (1) PREPRINT ONLY: the version read is the TechRxiv v1 posting, not the IEEE TMI version of record; this record belongs in the version-of-record sensitivity analysis exactly as 36200353 does in paper/screen/access_recovery.json. (2) INCOMPLETE DOCUMENT: the appendix the text refers to is absent from the preprint, so the 14-term negative is evidenced for the main text only.
